summary: The root "lmz" refers to someone who habitually blames, reproaches, or finds fault with others.
lane: لُمَزَةٌ ذ One who blames, upbraids, reproaches, or finds fault with, others, much, or habitually; (S, K;) as also , (so in two copies of the S, and in a copy of the A,) or , like سَحَابٌ : (K:) لُمَزَةٌ is applied to a man and to a woman; for its ة is to denote intensiveness, and not the fem. gender: (TA:) هُمَزَةٌ and لُمَزَةٌ signify the same; (ISk, Zj, K;) i. e., one who speaks evil of others, or does so in their absence, though it may be with truth; ( يَغْتَابُهُمْ ; and this may mean [ who detracts by making signs ] with the side of the mouth, or with the eye, or with the head; TA;) and defames them; (ISk, Zj, TA;) or one who often goes about with calumny, a separater of companions and friends: (Abu-l-'Abbás, TA:) and , like شَدَّادٌ , a frequent, or habitual, calumniator, or slanderer: (TA:) or هُمَزَةٌ and لُمَزَةٌ differ in signification; the latter signifying one who blames, upbraids, reproaches, or finds fault with, thee to thy face; and the former, one who does so in thine absence; (K;) and Lth says the like: (TA:) or the latter, one who speaks evil of others, though it may be with truth, ( مُغْتَابٌ ,) behind the back; and the former, one who does so to the face: or the latter, one who speaks against the lineages of men; and the former, one who speaks against the characters of men: or the latter, [one who reproaches ] with the tongue; and the former, with the eye: or the reverse: (K [but omitted in the CK], TA:) or the latter signifies one who excites discord, or animosity, between two persons. (TA.) See also هُمَزَةٌ . And see the Ksh and Bd in civ. 1.

headwords.gloss: He made a sign to him with the eye; the like; the head

parts.t: He made a sign to him with the eye,
(TA.) This is the original signification. (S, Msb, TA.) Hence, (S, Msb, TA,)
reproached, him; he found fault with him:
he did so in his face:
he met him with blaming, upbraiding, reproaching
spoke of him in a manner that he disliked, mentioning vices
either behind his back or before his face,
though it might be with truth;
. (TA.) The two forms of the aor. occur in readings of the words of the Kur., [ix. 58,]

headwords.def: لَمَزَهُ , aor. لَمِزَ and لَمُزَ , inf. n. لَمْزٌ , He made a sign to him with the eye, or the like, (S, A, * Msb, K,) as the head, and the lip, with low speech. (TA.) This is the original signification. (S, Msb, TA.) Hence, (S, Msb, TA,) He blamed, upbraided, or reproached, him; he found fault with him: (S, Msb, K:) or he did so in his face: (TA:) or he met him with blaming, upbraiding, reproaching or finding fault: (IKtt, TA:) or he spoke evil of him, or spoke of him in a manner that he disliked, mentioning vices or faults as chargeable to him, either behind his back or before his face, though it might be with truth; syn. إِغْتَابَهُ . (TA.) The two forms of the aor. occur in readings of the words of the Kur., [ix. 58,] وَمِنْهُمْ مَنْ يَلْمِزُكَ
